brief: c279: the garden has ONE budget across every weather, so every new way to be in it is paid for out of the others. #186 built the covered walk and measured it: set-outs 495 / 491 / 488 at stroll shares 0.20 / 0.12 / 0.07 — the arcade's walkers come out of the benches and the blankets, not out of inflow, because LAWN_CAP 8 is the bound. But #186 also measured that on a wet afternoon the benches are refused anyway: seatRefused() fired 237 times on weatherComing() > SIT_REFUSE, against 7 for the stop branch. So the covered walk should be paid by the WEATHER, not by the seats. Make the garden's inflow (LAWN_RATE, or LAWN_CAP, whichever is the slack bound — sweep and find out) read the weather, with the arcade the branch that survives it.
successLooksLike: In rain the courtyard is neither empty nor as full as a fine afternoon: the arcade holds people the lawn cannot. On a fine day the arcade's share falls back and the benches and blankets are no worse off than at #186 — quote the three set-out counts against #186's 495/491/488 on a pinned ref.
avoid: Do not raise LAWN_CAP flat. A bigger number in all weathers is the dimmer-switch answer, and LAWS says it plainly: hang the scalar on whichever bound is SLACK and prove it by sweeping the AXIS — the weather — not the constant. Also: a cap and a rate are only both alive if they bind at different times, so establish which one is actually binding on a wet day before you move either.
